inputs.statement: p is a prime number and K has characteristic p.

n=λ+1>0 and |I|=n. For every integer t≥0, h y^t v=(λ−2t)y^t v; for t≥1, x y^t v=t(λ−t+1)y^(t−1)v. The vectors (e_i)_{i∈I} form a complex basis of V, and y^(λ+1)v=0 (hence all higher lowering powers vanish). On this basis, xe_0=0, xe_i=(λ−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤λ, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for 0≤i<λ, ye_λ=0, he_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For all i∈I and natural r, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. All displayed divided-power coefficients are integers.

iota embeds M_R as the R-span of M in V; M_R is free of rank n over R and its complex span is V. Each X_r and Y_r (r≥0) preserves M and M_R, and x,y,h preserve M and M_R. For every i,j∈I, E_ij preserves M_R (under iota). The following identities hold on V: Pi=Y_λ X_λ=E_λλ, X_(λ−i)Pi=E_iλ, Pi Y_(λ−j)=binom(λ,j)E_λj, and E_ij=binom(λ,j)^(-1) X_(λ−i)Pi Y_(λ−j), where binom(λ,j) is a unit in R.

For every i∈I one has J_i=J. The R-module J⊂ℂ is nonzero and finitely generated. The map (c_i)_{i∈I}↦∑_{i∈I}c_i e_i is an R-linear isomorphism ∏_{i∈I}J→iota(M_R), so, identifying M_R through iota, M_R=⊕_{i∈I}J e_i.

output.statement: The multiplication map ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ is injective and its image is the rational span of J, a one-dimensional ℚ-vector space. There exists b∈J with b≠0 and J=Rb. For any such b, the family (b e_i)_{i∈I} is an R-basis of M_R identified with iota(M_R).

locals.declaration: Choose nonzero generators g_1,…,g_k of J.
Choose q_1,…,q_k∈ℚ^× such that g_j=q_j a.
For each q_j define eta_j=ν_j to be the exponent of p in its rational prime factorization.
Define u_j=p^(−eta_j)q_j. The assertion that these are units is proved in S004.

argument.text: Set QJ=ℚ⊗_R J. By N003, the tensors 1⊗c for any finite generating set c of J span QJ over ℚ, so QJ is finite-dimensional. Define the multiplication map on pure tensors by q⊗c↦qc∈ℂ. It is well-defined by R-balancing. Since ℚ is the fraction field of the subring R⊂ℚ (H001), every tensor is a finite sum of fractions times elements of J. A common nonzero denominator in R writes that entire tensor as s^(-1)⊗c with 0≠s∈R and c∈J. Its image is c/s; if this is zero in ℂ then c=0, so the tensor is zero. Thus the map is injective and identifies QJ with the rational span of J.

produces.statement: QJ is a finite-dimensional ℚ-vector space and multiplication QJ→ℂ is injective with image the rational span of J.

argument.text: Let r=dim_ℚ QJ. Apply M002 with source B=R, A=ℚ, C=M_R. The rings R and ℚ are nontrivial commutative domains and satisfy the strong rank condition: an injective finite matrix over R remains injective over ℚ by clearing denominators of a hypothetical kernel vector, and the dimension inequality over ℚ then gives the required rank inequality; the inclusion R→ℚ gives the algebra structure. N002 states that M_R is free of rank n, so M002 gives dim_ℚ(ℚ⊗_R M_R)=n. Tensoring the coordinate isomorphism of N003 gives ℚ⊗_R M_R≅∏_{i∈I}QJ: on a pure tensor with coordinates (c_i), the map sends q⊗(∑ c_i e_i) to (q⊗c_i)_i; inverse maps insert the coordinates and sum. These inverse maps are balanced and linear, so this identification needs no flatness assumption. Apply M001 with A=ℚ, B=I and constant family C_i=QJ. Here I is finite with |I|=n by N001; QJ is a finite-dimensional vector space by F001, hence free and finitely generated. We obtain dim_ℚ(∏_{i∈I}QJ)=∑_{i∈I}r=nr. Therefore n=nr. Since n>0 by N001, r=1.

Choose 0≠a∈J and a finite nonempty tuple g_1,…,g_k of nonzero generators of J, as permitted by N003. By F001 and F002, J lies in a one-dimensional rational line, and its nonzero vector a spans that line. Consequently each g_j=q_j a with a nonzero rational q_j. This proves the rational-coordinate description of a generating set; it is derived from the rank calculation rather than assumed merely from J⊂ℂ.

produces.statement: k≥1; a∈J is nonzero; g_1,…,g_k generate J and g_j=q_j a with q_j∈ℚ^× for 1≤j≤k.

argument.text: For each nonzero rational q_j, strip the factors p from its integer numerator and denominator. Since p is prime by H001, this gives q_j=p^(eta_j)u_j, with eta_j=ν_j∈ℤ and both numerator and denominator of u_j prime to p. Thus u_j and u_j^(-1) are in R. Put ν=min_j eta_j, which exists for the nonempty finite tuple of F003, and b=p^ν a≠0. Every generator q_j a=p^(eta_j−ν)u_j b belongs to Rb because eta_j−ν≥0. Conversely, for any generator attaining the minimum, multiplication of that generator by its unit u_j^(-1) gives b; hence b∈J and Rb⊆J. The first inclusion on generators gives J⊆Rb, so J=Rb.

N003 now gives M_R=⊕_{i∈I}Rb e_i. Its coordinate sum map shows that (b e_i) spans over R; since b≠0 and the e family is complex-linearly independent by N001, it is R-linearly independent. Thus it is an R-basis. The same reasoning works for any nonzero b with J=Rb. Together with F001 and F002 this proves the asserted rank and basis conclusions, exporting existence of such b without fixing its private identity.

hypothesis_checks: H001 and D007 make R a nontrivial commutative subring of ℚ. As explained at S002, clearing denominators preserves injectivity of a finite matrix on extension from R to ℚ; the vector-space dimension inequality over ℚ proves the strong rank condition for R. For ℚ that condition is the usual vector-space dimension inequality.
M_R is an R-module and is free of rank n by the direct input N002.
The inclusion R⊂ℚ is a unital ring map, giving the required R-algebra structure on ℚ.

applications.bindings: Take A=ℚ, B=I, and the constant family C_i=QJ=ℚ⊗_R J.
hypothesis_checks: ℚ is a field and therefore a semiring with the strong rank condition.
N001 gives |I|=n, so I is finite.
QJ is a ℚ-vector space by construction, hence has its additive commutative group and module structures.
F001, established at S001, proves QJ finite-dimensional; vector-space bases make it free, and finite dimension makes it finitely generated.
